analysis:
The supplied units are head-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1-801). The only changed range per file_changes is head 980-1027, a startup shape-warmup description, which falls outside both supplied excerpts (they end at line 801). The patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of that addition is not visible. I examined the visible unchanged surrounding text against the threat model and found no concrete security regression.

Nothing in the visible text weakens prefix-cache scoping (T-041/SEC-035). Text prefix reuse remains partitioned by authenticated cache scope, and without a scope it stays cold and never publishes. The Super slot emits no cache receipts. Nothing weakens the memory-admission, DoS or media-ingest bounds either (TB-007, T-028, T-029): the docs describe ingress and media charges before decode, an 8 MiB body cap, and 429/503 refusals.

From the patch excerpt, the new warmup runs on the provider's own synthetic prompts under a 20 s budget. It trains no rate or counter and has no described link to consumer data, keys or attestation. It is documentation only, so no controls change.

Residual question: the warmup's operational behavior (probe prompts, plaintext handling, whether warmup state could be observed as a timing signal across tenants) is documented in a part of the patch not visible here, and the cited ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift source was not supplied. I cannot confirm that no consumer content enters warmup or that the real code matches the docs, so a deeper pass over that code is advisable but not required by any observed issue.
